An attacker on HTTP can perform a cross-site POST form submission; SameSite=Lax does not prevent cookies on top-level cross-origin form POSTs, and the server will trust the cookie to trigger a webhook test.

extra.message: Audit-log endpoint exposes client IP addresses

metadata.citation: return [{"id": a.id, "actor": a.actor.full_name if a.actor else "system", "action": a.action, "entity_type": a.entity_type, "entity_id": a.entity_id, "summary": a.summary, "ip_address": a.ip_address, "created_at": a.created_at.isoformat()} for a in db.scalars(stmt).all()]
metadata.proof: The /api/admin/audit endpoint (line 785) returns the ip_address field stored in every audit log entry. Although restricted to ops_admin users, IP addresses are PII and are returned without any data minimization or need-to-know filter, exposing all client IPs to any admin caller.

extra.message: Registration endpoint has no rate limiting

metadata.proof: The registration handler at line 281 creates portal users with no throttling, IP-based rate limit, or CAPTCHA. An attacker can mass-register accounts to exhaust storage/processing or enumerate valid customer_id values by observing 422 vs 409 responses.

extra.message: API-key integration endpoint has no rate limiting

metadata.proof: The /api/integrations/job-status endpoint at line 922 validates the x-api-key header by SHA-256 hashing it and comparing against stored hashes. There is no rate limiting or account lockout, allowing an attacker to brute-force API keys over the network. SHA-256 is also a fast hash, providing no brute-force resistance if the hashes are ever leaked.

extra.message: Missing region scoping on list_customers — dispatchers can enumerate all customers' PII across regions

metadata.citation:
customers = db.scalars(select(Customer).order_by(Customer.company_name)).all()
return [{"id": c.id, "company_name": c.company_name, "contact_name": c.contact_name, "contact_email": c.contact_email, "contact_phone": c.contact_phone} for c in customers if c]
metadata.proof: The `list_customers` endpoint (GET /api/customers) at line 698-707 returns ALL customers with PII (contact_name, contact_email, contact_phone) to any dispatcher without applying the region filter that every other endpoint enforces for dispatchers (e.g., job_query_for_user at line 146 adds `Job.region_id == user.region_id`; list_routes at line 674 adds `Route.region_id == user.region_id`; bootstrap at line 342 adds `User.region_id == user.region_id`; list_locations at line 726 adds `ServiceLocation.region_id == user.region_id`). A dispatcher in region "North" can enumerate contact details of customers exclusively served by region "South". The untrusted SOURCE is the user's role (dispatcher) allowing access; the SINK is `select(Customer).all()` returning the full dataset without any region predicate.

extra.message: Unvalidated file content-type — client-provided Content-Type stored and served without server-side verification

metadata.proof: The `file.content_type` value is taken from the HTTP request's Content-Type header (untrusted client input — SOURCE) at line 571, stored in the database, and later served as `media_type` in `FileResponse` (line 597, GET /api/proofs/{proof_id}/download — SINK). No server-side magic-byte or MIME validation is performed. A field worker can upload a `.html` file that spoofs Content-Type: text/html; the file is stored with the `.html` extension (from `safe_suffix`), and when downloaded the browser may render it as HTML, enabling stored XSS against any user who views the file (including ops_admins). Conversely, an `.exe` with Content-Type: image/png bypasses client-side filters.

extra.message: Information disclosure via discrepant error messages in proof download — cross-tenant proof existence oracle

metadata.proof: The proof is fetched via `db.get(ProofUpload, proof_id)` at line 584 without any user/tenant scope check. Four different error messages are emitted depending on state: (1) 'Proof not found' if proof_id doesn't exist; (2) 'Job not found' from `get_visible_job` at line 587 if the proof exists but belongs to another customer's job; (3) 'Proof not found' at line 590 if job is visible but proof is not customer_visible; (4) 'Stored file missing' at line 593 if proof is visible but file is absent. A customer can brute-force proof_ids — different responses reveal whether a proof_id exists, which customer it belongs to, and whether the file is present on disk — enabling cross-tenant proof existence enumeration. The SOURCE is the user-supplied `proof_id` path parameter; the SINK is the cascading error-message branch logic.

extra.message: User enumeration via registration endpoint — divergent HTTP 409 for existing email

metadata.proof: POST /api/auth/register returns HTTP 409 with 'Email already registered' when the email exists (line 285), HTTP 200 when the email is new with a valid customer_id, and HTTP 422 when the email is new with an invalid customer_id. An unauthenticated attacker can enumerate registered email addresses by observing the distinct status codes. The SOURCE is the untrusted request body (`payload.email`); the SINK is the conditional branch at line 284 that produces different HTTP statuses based on email existence.

extra.message: IDOR in CSV job import — location resolved by label only, enabling cross-customer job creation

metadata.proof: The CSV import for 'jobs' resolves the ServiceLocation by label alone at line 822 without scoping to the customer. If Customer A and Customer B both have a location labeled 'Main Site', importing a job row with `customer=CustomerA` and `location_label=Main Site` can resolve to Customer B's location (the first row returned). The job is then created with Customer A's customer_id but Customer B's location_id (and its region_id), producing a cross-tenant record that links one customer's job to another customer's location. The SOURCE is the untrusted CSV file content; the SINK is the unscoped `select(ServiceLocation)...` query followed by `Job(... location_id=location.id...)` creation at lines 828-830.

extra.message: Missing authorization — field worker can assign incidents to arbitrary users without validation

metadata.proof: POST /api/incidents (lines 611-627) accepts `assigned_to_id` from the request body (untrusted SOURCE). The value is passed directly to the Incident constructor at line 619 without any validation that the assignee is a dispatcher/ops_admin, belongs to the same region, or is even an active user. A field worker can assign an incident to a customer portal user, a field worker in a different region, or any arbitrary user ID (SINK), circumventing the intended incident-handling workflow. While the endpoint does verify the job is visible (line 612) and that field workers can only report for their own jobs (line 614), there is zero validation on who the incident is assigned to.

extra.message: User enumeration via registration response

metadata.proof: POST /api/auth/register queries the database for the email and returns 409 only when the account exists, while successful registration returns 200. The divergent status code lets an attacker probe whether any email address is registered.

extra.message: Cross-customer directory disclosure in bootstrap for field workers/dispatchers

metadata.proof: GET /api/bootstrap runs this unfiltered query for every authenticated user except customers. A field_worker or dispatcher receives the full customer directory, not only customers they serve, leaking cross-org customer names and IDs.

extra.message: Cross-customer location disclosure for field workers

metadata.proof: GET /api/locations for a field_worker filters only by the worker's region_id. Any service location in that region is returned regardless of which customer owns it, so a worker can read other customers' site addresses within the same region.

extra.message: Uploaded proof documents stored unencrypted

metadata.proof: POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/proofs writes the raw uploaded bytes directly to the local upload directory via write_bytes(). Sensitive proof files (signatures, photos, completion documents) are persisted on disk without any encryption, exposing them to anyone with filesystem access.

extra.message: Unbounded memory buffering in CSV export

metadata.proof: GET /api/export/{kind} loads all matching jobs, incidents, or routes into an in-memory list, then csv_response() materializes the entire CSV in a StringIO via iter([output.getvalue()]). An authenticated user can request an export large enough to exhaust server memory.

extra.message: Password reset does not revoke existing sessions

metadata.proof: POST /api/auth/password-reset/confirm changes the user's hashed_password but does not maintain a token revocation list or increment a password version. Any previously issued JWT session cookie remains valid for its full TTL, so an attacker who stole a token keeps access after the legitimate user resets the password.

extra.message: API keys are non-expiring and cannot be revoked through the API

metadata.proof: POST /api/admin/api-keys creates an ApiKey with only created_at and active, no expiry column, and there is no DELETE or deactivate endpoint for keys. A leaked integration key remains valid indefinitely until manual database intervention.
